title: Python Virtual Environments
subtitle: Keep every project's packages separate with venv
author: doc-studio test

summary.topic: What a Python virtual environment is, and how to create, use and share one with the built-in venv module (Python 3.3+).
key_points: A venv gives each project its own packages, so projects don't break each other
Create it with `python -m venv .venv`, then activate it

slides.title: The problem venv solves
left: All projects share one set of packages
Upgrading for project A can break project B
Hard to tell what a project really needs
right: Each project has its own packages
requirements.txt lists exactly what it needs
slides.notes: Start with a story: two projects needing different versions of the same library.

slides.title: What's inside a project
slides.caption: Diagram: AI-drawn for this deck
slides.notes: The .venv folder holds a Python interpreter and its own site-packages. The docs say it is conventionally named .venv or venv.

slides.title: Create and activate
slides.text: Run in your project folder (venv is built in since Python 3.3):
slides.code:
# create
python -m venv .venv

# activate: macOS / Linux (bash, zsh)
source .venv/bin/activate

# activate: Windows PowerShell
.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1

# activate: Windows cmd.exe
.venv\Scripts\activate.bat
slides.caption: Commands from the Python docs (docs.python.org/3/library/venv.html)
slides.notes: On Windows PowerShell the execution policy may need changing first; the docs show the Set-ExecutionPolicy command.

slides.title: Install and record packages
slides.text: With the venv active, pip installs into the venv only:
slides.code:
python -m pip install requests

# save the exact versions
python -m pip freeze > requirements.txt

# later, or on another computer
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
slides.caption: Commands from the pip user guide (pip.pypa.io)

slides.title: Golden rules from the docs
bullets: Treat it as disposable: delete and recreate it
Don't copy it to another computer: it isn't portable
Keep your code outside the .venv folder
slides.notes: All five come from the 'How venvs work' section of the venv docs.

slides.title: Common mistakes
right: Add .venv to .gitignore (3.13+ adds one inside the venv for you)
Recreate it and run pip install -r

slides.title: Try it now
bullets: Make a new folder and create a .venv
Activate it and install one package
Delete .venv, recreate it, reinstall from the file
slides.notes: Five-minute exercise. Ask learners to show their requirements.txt.
